page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-8 is an ARM-based virtual machine instance powered by the ARMv8 architecture. It features 8 dedicated physical cores utilizing the Neoverse-V2 processor model, running at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU acceleration included with this instance type. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 80 MB of L3 cache.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4a-standard-8 demonstrates strong memory performance, with its PassMark memory score reaching the top tier. Read-only memory bandwidth for large blocks is particularly strong at 198.51 GB/sec, while small-block cached reads average 984.48 GB/sec. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks show strong results, with gzip compression reaching 32.3 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.14 GB/sec. However, cryptographic performance is a notable tradeoff, with the PassMark CPU encryption test scoring in the weak tier at 1665.96. Standard compute workloads, such as stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, deliver average performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4a-standard-8 offers a competitive resource density for ARM-native workloads, delivering top-tier memory performance and balanced compute without the overhead of hyperthreading. This makes it suitable for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, database operations, and lightweight language model inference. It is designed for applications that benefit from high memory bandwidth and dedicated physical cores, though workloads heavily reliant on hardware-accelerated cryptography may experience performance limitations.
